THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 19.02.2020 PASSED IN MVC NO.498/2019 BY III ADDITIONAL DISTRICT JUDGE AND MACT,
MYSURU AND ETC.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by the appellant-claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 19.02.2020 passed in MVC.No.498/2019 by the Court of III Additional District Judge and MACT,
Mysuru (for short 'the tribunal').

entities.text:
Court of III Additional District Judge and MACT,
Mysuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appeal is preferred on the premise of inadequate and meager compensation awarded by the tribunal.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case is as under:
On 13.02.2019 at about 11.00 p.m., the claimant after completing his work, was going back to his house on his two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-45-L-6745 and when he was proceeding near the residence of Karishettygowda within the limits of his village, a Tata Ace NC: 2024:KHC:2026 Goods Auto bearing registration No.KA-45-4324 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came from behind and dashed against the rear side of the two wheeler of the claimant, as a result, the claimant sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately shifted to Apollo Hospital, Mysuru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient for four days and underwent surgery and expended Rs.5,00,000/-.
3.1 It is stated that the claimant was hale and healthy prior to the occurrence of accident.
He was doing coolie work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained, he is unable to do his work as he was doing prior to the accident.

He has suffered disability, which restrains him from progressing in his life,
profession and even otherwise.
Due to the said impact, the Police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the offending goods vehicle.
Hence, the claimant filed a claim petition seeking compensation.

On service of notice, the respondents filed statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition including age, avocation, income and negligence Sri Basavaraju vs Mahesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167324730/
2 attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.3 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
3.4 In order to substantiate the issue and to establish the case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1, the Doctor as PW.2 and another witness as PW.3 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P16.

On the other hand, respondents examined witnesses as RWs.1 and 2 and got marked documents as Exs.R1 to R4.
3.5

On the basis of material evidence produced by the parties, the tribunal awarded the compensation of Rs.5,25,200/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed respondent No.2 to pay the compensation within two months.
Being aggrieved by the meager compensation amount awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

4. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and reasonable compensation and has ignored the expert evidence of PW.2-Doctor and reduced the disability to the extent of 7%, which calls for interference at the hands of this Court.
On these grounds, he seeks enhancement of the compensation awarded by the tribunal.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company vehemently contends that there is no error and discrepancy in the judgment and award of the tribunal.
The tribunal has rightly taken the notional income so also disability.
PW.2-Doctor has not effectively assessed or opined or expressed the disability towards upper and lower limbs.
Under the circumstances, he sustains the NC: 2024:KHC:2026 impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal.
On these grounds, he seeks for dismissal of the appeal.

6. Having heard learned counsel for appellant- claimant and respondent-Insurance Company and perused the impugned judgment and award and evidence adduced by the parties, it is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 13.02.2019 and involvement of two vehicles.

To establish the same,
the claimant has produced the documents as Exs.P1 to P8, the Police records, which clearly disclose the laying of chargesheet against the driver of the offending vehicle, which is not disputed or challenged.
Exs. P9 to P16, the medical records clearly indicate the injuries encountered by the claimant pursuant to the occurrence of accident.

This clearly goes to show that the negligence has been rightly attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle and the same does not call for interference.
7.

Now coming to the age, avocation and income of the claimant as on the date of occurrence of accident, the NC: 2024:KHC:2026 tribunal taken the income of Rs.9,000/- per month, in view of there being no proof of income.
However, Legal Services Authority chart stipulates the notional income of Rs.14,000/- for the accident of the year 2019 and accordingly, the same is taken in this case.
The age of the claimant is 36 years.

The appropriate multiplier would be '15', which is rightly Sri Basavaraju vs Mahesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167324730/
3 applied by the tribunal, which does not call for interference.

sentences.text: The disability assessed by PW.2- Doctor is to an extent of 22% to the right lower limb and 12% to the right upper limb, which in all comes to 34%.
However, he has not expressed any opinion with regard to the disability to the whole body.

As per the Government of India Gazette notification, the disability has to be calculated as 34% x 1/3rd,
which would come to 11.3%. Therefore, the disability is assessed at 11% as against 7% assessed by the tribunal.

Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to the compensation of Rs.2,77,200/-
(Rs.14,000/- x 12 x 15 x 11%) towards loss of future income as against Rs.1,19,700/- awarded by the tribunal.

The tribunal awarded Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.2,80,000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.10,000/- towards food and nourishment, Rs.10,000/- towards transportation charges,
Rs.2,000/- towards attendant charges, which do not call for interference and the same are retained.
9.
The tribunal awarded Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities in life.
This Court deems it appropriate to award additional amount of Rs.20,000/-.
In all, Rs.45,000/- is awarded under this head.
10. The tribunal awarded Rs.28,500/- towards loss of income during laid up period.
In view of this Court enhancing the income from Rs.9,000/- to Rs.14,000/-, the claimant would require atleast three months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.42,000/- (Rs.14,000/- x 3) under this head.
In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,16,200/- as against Rs.5,25,200/- as mentioned in the table below:

Heads Amount in Rs.
Pain and suffering 50,000-00 Medical expenses 2,80,000-00
Food and nourishment 10,000-00 Transportation charges 10,000-00 Loss of amenities in life 45,000-00
Attendant charges 2,000-00
Loss of future income 2,77,200-00 Loss of income during laid up period 42,000-00
TOTAL 7,16,200-00 Sri Basavaraju vs Mahesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167324730/
